equity_bridge.item: FY2026 income tax payable (residual 15% of FY26 liability, settled H1 FY27)
equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR balance sheet, current liabilities; a claim on the A$252m cash pile that the forward tax line does not capture

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Near-term EPP revenue growth judgment: revenue 3yr CAGR 6.3% tempered by FY2026 -1% (H2 FY26 -4% YoY on an AUD headwind and flat US patient adds); base year-1 3%, years 2-4 4-5%. Equity CAGR (18-22%) is rejected as the anchor: it measures retention of a cash pile that pays 5c/share out of 68c earned, not business growth.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 22.5% diverges >30% from revenue 14.4% and EPS 6.3%. Cause: near-zero payout ratio accumulating cash and term deposits (A$121.5m FY22 -> A$252.1m FY26), so book value compounds faster than the business. Not used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY21 15.5, FY22 32.9, FY23 23.0, FY24 18.0, FY25 29.4, FY26 22.5. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (7.8%) sits well below reported (13.9%) because interest income grew from A$0.3m to A$10.4m, not because SBC grew: SBC peaked at A$9.0m in FY23 and is now A$2.3m. FY26 owner FCF is additionally depressed ~A$7.6m by the ATO PAYG tax prepayment.

scenario_narratives.base: SCENESSE remains the only approved EPP therapy and grows low-to-mid single digits on North American center expansion, Canadian reimbursement and the EMA year-round dosing label, while AUD strength and a mature European base cap the rate. The vitiligo program (CUV105 topline late CY2026, CUV107 to follow) reaches a dossier around FY2029-30 and contributes modestly from FY2031, at a small fraction of management's US$450-570m year-1/2 estimate. EBITDA margin drifts from 44% to 42% as the US team, Nasdaq listing and Phase III spend absorb leverage, then recovers to 45%. The A$252m cash pile is credited at face after the A$6.7m tax payable.
scenario_narratives.bull: CUV105 reads out positive, CUV107 confirms, and systemic repigmentation for vitiligo (skin types IV-VI) is approved and launched around FY2030-31 through the specialty-center network already built for EPP, reaching ~A$150m by FY2035. EPP itself grows 5-10% toward the US$300m TAM as year-round dosing lifts implants per patient. NEURACTHEL and PhotoCosmetics add small lines. Margins expand to 50% on shared infrastructure. Revenue ~A$310m by FY2036.
scenario_narratives.bear: The single-product dependency bites: an oral MC1R agonist competitor takes EPP share, European growth stalls and AUD strength compresses reported revenue 2-3%/yr. CUV105 is equivocal, the vitiligo program never reaches regulators, and management continues to spend the cash pile on the diversification pipeline, the US build-out and the Nasdaq move with no revenue payoff, so EBITDA margin compresses from 44% to 32%. Terminal growth 0%, 12x cap. The cash pile still supports the value, which is why the bear case is not far below the price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the EPP franchise as a mature, highly cash-generative single-product business, strip the interest on the cash pile from the flows and add the cash back once, and treat vitiligo as scenario optionality rather than a risked NPV. At A$8.25 the market pays ~A$168m EV for a business earning ~A$40m of operating EBIT: the market is pricing either franchise erosion or the cash being spent badly, and the 30% bear weight is where that view lives in this model.
key_risks_to_valuation: Single-product concentration: SCENESSE for EPP is essentially all product revenue; an approved oral MC1R agonist competitor would erode the base directly.
CUV105 topline (late CY2026) is a binary that moves the bull weight; a negative read-out also removes the main use for the cash pile.

Capital allocation: A$252m of cash reserves, ~5c/share dividend on 68c EPS, no buyback, and a stated intent to fund a multi-product pipeline plus a Nasdaq primary listing from reserves; the DCF credits the cash at face.
FX: revenue is earned in EUR/USD and reported in AUD; FY2026 carried a A$4.0m unrealised FX loss on cash balances.
Key-person dependency on the CEO (agreement extended March 2026) and a history of governance friction with shareholders.

data_sources.financials: CUV.AX_Metrics.csv (FY2016-FY2026 annual + half-years); FY2026 Annual Report (income statement, balance sheet, cash-flow statement, note 14 EPS, note 15(b) reconciliation, chairman's cash-reserves letter)
data_sources.qualitative: FY2026 Annual Report operating review, 'Melanocortin House' market slide (EPP US$64m revenue vs US$300m TAM; vitiligo US$450-570m year-1/2 estimate), chairman's three-year milestones; CUV.AX_Analysis.json not yet available at build time

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average shares FY2026 (EPS note 14: 50,009,944 basic + 736,935 performance rights = 50,746,879). 50,427,898 shares on issue at 30 Jun 2026. Held FLAT: SBC (performance rights) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would double-charge. No non-SBC issuance in the last decade; company states expansion is funded from cash reserves, not raisings.
inputs.cash_note: Cash and cash equivalents A$21.392m + cash held in term deposits A$230.664m = A$252.055m ('cash reserves', the company's own non-IFRS measure) at 30 Jun 2026. Total debt is lease liabilities only (A$0.389m current + A$1.550m non-current); no borrowings for the twentieth consecutive year.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF A$36.910m less PP&E capex A$1.602m. Depressed by the ATO PAYG transition: cash tax paid A$23.365m vs A$13.743m expense (A$14m FY25 liability plus ~85% prepayment of FY26). On a like-for-like tax basis reported FCF would be ~A$43m and owner FCF ~A$30m (~32% of revenue), which is what the component build converges to.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report cash-flow reconciliation note 15(b), 'Share-based payment' A$2,338,206 (FY2025 A$2,001,467). Equity-award taxes nil: 'Payments related to employee share schemes' A$0.564m is exactly offset by the matching issuance line. SBC fell from A$8.99m (FY23, 11.5% of revenue) after the performance-rights restructure; 2.5% is the current run-rate.
inputs.buyback_note: No buyback in FY2026. FY2025 A$0.252m and FY2024 A$0.754m were the only repurchases in the history; a A$2.5m/yr (5c/share) unfranked dividend is the only capital return. The flat count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for, but at 2.5% SBC the cost is small.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows, AUD discount rate. Australian 10yr ACGB ~4.4% + beta 1.15 x 5.5% ERP = ~10.7% cost of equity, used as 10.5% WACC; the company is debt-free so WACC = cost of equity. No ad-hoc single-product premium is stacked on top: SCENESSE concentration, the CUV105/CUV107 vitiligo binary and the capital-allocation risk on the A$252m cash pile are charged once, in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight (section 7f). One WACC across all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities A$1.938m are inside total_debt; lease principal (A$0.239m FY26) is NOT deducted from the flows; ROU depreciation stays inside D&A and lease-asset renewal is carried inside the 2.0% capex line. The lease is 0.25% of revenue so the choice is immaterial, but it is stated once.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, specialty pharma with one approved product). Not routed to a pre-revenue/risked-NPV model because SCENESSE (EPP) is a ten-year profitable franchise; the vitiligo binary is handled as scenario optionality on top of the EPP base rather than as a risked NPV. Interest income (A$10.4m, 11% of revenue) is stripped from the flows and the A$252m cash pile is added back once in the bridge (matching-asset rule). Revenue in the CSV (A$94.0m) is product sales + reimbursements and EXCLUDES interest income; the A$104.5m 'total revenues' in the chairman's framing includes it. Cash tax modelled at the 30% Australian statutory rate (FY26 effective 28.8%, FY25 29.8%); the FY26 prepayment reverses in H1 FY27 and is not projected. Working capital: receivables + inventory less payables = A$21m (22% of revenue), so growth consumes cash; wc_capture negative. Equity bridge deducts the A$6.7m FY26 income-tax payable still owed at 30 Jun 2026.

bear.growth_note: EPP franchise erodes: an oral MC1R agonist competitor (e.g. dersimelagon) reaches the EPP market, European patient base plateaus, AUD stays strong; CUV105 topline is equivocal and the vitiligo program never reaches a dossier. No new revenue lines.
bear.margin_note: Management keeps spending the cash pile on the 'house of melanocortins' (CUV107, NEURACTHEL, VLRX-L, PhotoCosmetics, US build-out, Nasdaq) with no revenue payoff, so opex rises against a shrinking base: margin compresses to ~32%. This is how the capital-allocation risk on A$252m is charged in the flows.

base.growth_note: Years 1-4: EPP only. US specialty centers 134 and growing, Canada reimbursement building, EMA year-round dosing label lifting implants per patient, offset by AUD strength and a maturing European base. Years 5-8: a heavily risked vitiligo contribution from ~FY2031 (CUV105 topline late CY2026, CUV107 second Phase III, dossier ~FY2029-30, launch FY2031), worth ~A$45m incremental by FY2034 against the company's US$450-570m year-1/2 US estimate; i.e. roughly 5-8% of management's own number.
base.margin_note: FY26 44.2% (income from operations 40.5 + D&A 1.0 on 94.0). Drifts to 42% as the US team, Nasdaq primary-listing costs and CUV107 R&D absorb operating leverage, then recovers to 45% as vitiligo scales on the same infrastructure.
base.capex_note: 3yr average PP&E capex 2.8% of revenue (FY24 6.3% Singapore/US build, FY25 0.3%, FY26 1.7%); 2.0% covers maintenance plus lease-asset renewal under treatment (A).
base.cap_note: 15x rather than the 20x default: a single-product specialty pharma whose orphan exclusivities have largely run off and whose franchise depends on the implant formulation and the absence of an approved oral competitor.

bull.growth_note: EPP grows 5-10% (US penetration toward the US$300m TAM, year-round dosing), CUV105 positive, CUV107 completes, vitiligo approved and launched ~FY2030-31 reaching ~A$150m by FY2035 (still only ~20% of the company's US$450-570m year-1/2 estimate). NEURACTHEL and PhotoCosmetics add modest lines. Revenue ~A$310m by FY2036.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% for single-product revenue concentration (SCENESSE is ~100% of product revenue), a live oral-competitor threat in EPP, FY2026's first revenue decline, and a governance/capital-allocation overhang on a A$252m cash pile that management intends to deploy rather than return. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right: CUV105 positive, CUV107 funded and positive, regulatory approval, and a commercial launch in a large indication the company has never sold into. Base 45%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
